title: Search for a target encoding
statement: Let $x$ be a finite Boolean word, $B$ a natural number, and $q$ a rational number. Let $d$ be a natural number and $\sigma$ a register state such that $\sigma.n-\sigma.u=d$, every register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$, $\sigma.u\le\sigma.n$, $\sigma.t=0$, $\sigma.q\le |x|$, and $2|x|+2\le B$. Assume that for every $j$ with $\sigma.u\le j<\sigma.n$ whose binary word occurs at position $\sigma.q$ in $x$ and ends exactly at the end of $x$, the program started at the candidate-processing stage with $u=t=j$, pointer $|x|$, and scratch value zero has semantics with acceptance probability $q$. If there is no such $j$, assume $q=0$. Then the program started at the search stage in state $\sigma$ has semantics with acceptance probability $q$.
hypotheses_covered: Every register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$
For every qualifying $j$, the stated candidate-processing configuration has semantics with acceptance probability $q$
If there is no qualifying $j$, then $q=0$

program started at the indicated candidate-processing stage with registers $u=t=j$,
pointer $|x|$, and scratch value zero has semantics with acceptance probability $q$. If
there is no such $j$, assume $q=0$. Then the program started at the search stage in
state $\sigma$ has semantics with acceptance probability $q$.
